out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: DOK Time and Temp Req
violations.observation: Employees available for questioning on shift are not knowledgeable of proper cold holding temperatures or procedures on how to cool foods to proper cold holding temperature.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge shall know the following: 1) Cold foods shall be stored at 41F or below, 2) Hot foods shall be held at 135F or above, 3) Foods for cooling shall be rapidly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F or below within a total of 6 hours, and 4) Foods shall be reheated to an internal temperature of above 165F if prepared on site or above 135F if commercially processed. EHS instructed and demonstrated proper cooling technique for foods meant to be cold held that were within cooling time window.

out_items.name: Certified Food Protection Manager

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. No CFM present during inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. Additional staff must obtain CFM. A follow up inspection will be conducted on or around 10 days to verify a CFM is present during all hours of operation.

out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: Minimize Bare Hand/Arm Contact with Non-RTE Foods
violations.observation: Excessive bare hand contact with exposed food that is not in a ready-to-eat form. Observed employee take gloved hand and grab cut vegetables from 2 DR PREP and place into stockpot for cooking into soup.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed food that is NOT in a ready-to-eat food. Foods like sugar, salt, flour, starch, etc. shall be dispensed using food scoops or utensils that are designed with handles to minimize bare hand contact. EHS recommended placing and using tongs/utensils in each container at prep table to portion food during preparation.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: Observed hand sink in women’s restroom with a maximum hot water temperature of 80F.
violations.corrective_action: A handwashing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed soiled cook ware stored in basin of hand sink located next to prep sink.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EHS discussed with employee that hand sinks are only to be used for hand washing.

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Records, Parasite Destruction by Freezing
violations.observation: No records of freezing for parasite destruction are maintained for the following raw, raw marinated, partially cooked or marinated-partially cooked fish that are served or sold in ready-to-eat form: octopus in TAKO WASABI.
violations.corrective_action: If raw or partially cooked fish are served or sold in ready-to-eat form, the person in charge shall record the freezing temperature and time to which the fish are subjected and shall retain the records for the frozen fish at the food establishment for 90 calendar days beyond the time of service or sale to a consumer. If the fish are frozen by a supplier, a letter the fish supplier stipulating that the fish is frozen as required shall be provided. Employee stated that they are currently not serving any raw octopus due to a recall. EHS informed them that a parasite destruction letter will need to be requested from supplier before continuing to offer raw octopus on menu.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Cover Foods in Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped or uncovered food in the following location where the food is subject to contamination: pot of cooked soup observed on floor next to hand washing sink.
violations.corrective_action: Foods shall be protected from contamination by being stored in packages, covered containers or wrappings unless being cooled. Employee moved soup to stovetop.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Surfaces of ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment are not being cleaned as required. Observed accumulation of grime and mold-like substance on interior of ice machine.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. Clean interior of ice machine of grime and mold-like substance.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: bean sprouts in room temperature water at 70F, raw shell egg scramble in shallow pan of ice at 56F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS instructed and demonstrated to employees: the addition of ice to container of bean sprouts to cool to 41F and to submerge container of egg scramble in ice bath to cool entire container to 41F.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: stock pot of soup with date marking of 6/30, container of marinated soft boiled eggs with date marking of 7/3.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. Employee relabeled containers with correct date of 7/13. KIMEN (Inspection Date: 07/14/2026) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Observed boxes and packages of food, oil on floor of kitchen and walk in freezer, walk in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. Food must be stored at least 6 inches off floor. Move foods to shelves.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equipment/Utensils Air Drying
violations.observation: Observed plastic and stainless steel containers stacked and stored while wet after cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining before contact with food.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed accumulation of dust, food debris throughout floors, walls, and ceilings (ceiling vents, hood vents).
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. Clean all areas of food and dust debris. KIMEN (Inspection Date: 07/14/2026) Page 3 of 4

violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage No Contamination
violations.observation: Food stored in a location where it is subject to splash, dust or other contamination as follows: observed stockpots of soup stored underneath and next to hand sink located at cookline/dish area.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination. CFM and PIC moved rotated dunnage rack storing soups parallel to cookline equipment. Soups stored there for cooling are no longer directly underneath hand sink.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: DOK Time and Temp
violations.observation: There is no certified food manager on duty and the person in charge was unable to explain the significance of the relationship between maintaining the time and temperature of time/temperature control for safety food items and the prevention of foodborne disease.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge shall be aware that foodborne illness can be caused by temperature abuse of foods, especially if left out at room temperature for extended periods of time. Cold foods shall remain at 41F or below and hot foods at 135For above.

out_items.name: Certified Food Protection Manager

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. There was no certified food manager present.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. A CFM must be present during all hours of operation.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: DOK Employee Health Policy
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide a verbal or written policy for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by an employee who has a disease or a medical condition. The employee wasn’t’ able to provide an employee health policy
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge or certified food manager is responsible for knowledge, of at least the primary foodborne diseases (the Big 6) and medical conditions, to determine possible restriction or exclusion of food employees. The EHS provided the employee with the model FCHD employee health policy. The employee made copies and had each food employee review and sign a copy.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: in the walk-in refrigerator and freezer , raw animal foods were not stored properly and according to cook temperature. Raw shrimp was stored under raw chicken and raw chicken was stored over raw beef.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature).

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure: there are several menu items such as Tantannen, Miso Ramen, Mazemen, and Yaki Soba which have asterisks, but the asterisk is not placed next to the food ingredients that are served raw or under cooked. Also, a statement stating these items are served raw or undercooked does not appear on the menu.
violations.corrective_action: The Consumer Advisory shall include a disclosure statement that includes a description of the animal-derived foods as raw/undercooked or identification of the animal-derived foods by asterisking (*) them to a footnote that states that the items are served raw or undercooked, or contain raw or undercooked ingredients. update the menus so that the consumer advisory asterisks are placed next to the ingredient(s) that are served raw or undercooked. Also include a statement stating these items are served raw or undercooked. An asterisk alone is not sufficient. Place asterisk next to “seasoned egg”.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Storage of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Observed chemicals such as butane, bottles of cleaning solutions, spray bottles of cleaning solutions and other chemicals stored improperly with food, equipment and single service items.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored below food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items to prevent contamination. All chemicals must be stored separate from food, food equipment and single service items.

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. Observed a spray bottle of cleaning solution used to clean the grill with no label.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. Provide a label for the spray bottle.

out_items.name: Compliance with variance, specialized process, HACCP

violations.title: ROP, HACCP Plan in Place
violations.observation: The establishment is using reduced oxygen packaging and sous vide method to cook raw chicken. The product is called chasu chicken. The establishment does not have an approved HACCP plan for this product that is packaged using the Reduced Oxygen Packaging (ROP) process.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment that packages a time/temperature control for safe food using a Reduced Oxygen Packaging method shall have a HACCP plan that contains the information specified under 8-201.14(D) and that: 1) identifies the food to be packaged, 2) requires that the packaged food shall be maintained at 41F or less, has a water activity of 0.91 or less, a pH of 4.6 or less, is a meat or poultry product that is cured at a food processing plant, is received in an intact package, or is a food with a high level of competing organisms, 3) describes how the package shall be prominently and conspicuosly labeled on the principal display panel in bold type on a contrasting background with instructions to maintain the food at 41F or below and discard the food if within 14 calendar days of its packaging, 40 limits the refrigerated shelf life to no more than 14 calendar days from packaging to consumption or the origjnal manufacturer's 'sell by' or 'use by' date whichever occurs first, 5) includes operational procedures that prohibit contacting food with bare hands, identifies a designated work area and the method by which physical barriers or methods of separation minimizes cross contamination, access to the processing equipment is limited to responsible trained personnel, and cleaning and sanitizing procedures for equipment/utensils is monitored, and 6) describes the training program that ensures that the individual responsible for the ROP operation understands the concepts required for a safe operation, understands the equipment and facilites, and procedures specified in this section. EHS spoke with CFM over phone and sous vide chicken process will be discontinued.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: food employees were cooling large 5-gallon pots of hot soup at a room temperature in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. The EHS told the food employees to transfer pots of soup to the walk-in freezer and stir them every 10 minutes. KIMEN (Inspection Date: 07/31/2025) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Food Thermometers Accuracy, Only Degrees F
violations.observation: The food temperature measuring device is not accurate in degrees F. The food thermometer provided to the EHS by the food employees was not accurate and was not the correct scale.
violations.corrective_action: Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to +/- 2 degrees F in the intended range of use. Provide new thermometers that can display temperatures in plus or minus 2 degrees.

violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location. EHS had employees move soup pots to freezer.

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor

violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage.

violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Smooth, Easily Cleanable
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not finished to have a smooth, cleanable surface: observed plastic grocery store baskets being used to store cooked eggs.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be finished to have a smooth, easily cleanable surface. out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: Raw meats observed stored over broth in walk in cooler

Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: -Bean sprouts in ambient (65F) -Kimchi in 1 Dr countertop (60F)
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. -Discussed to keep bean sprouts on ice or in cooler unit. out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food
violations.observation: A review of the menu with the foodservice operator indicates that there is no consumer advisory for the following food item(s) that may be served raw and/or undercooked: Tako wasabi, Kimen ramen, Kimen spicy ramen, Shoyo ramen, Miso ramen, Tantan, Mazeman
violations.corrective_action: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw or undercooked the permit holder shall inform consumers of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. New menus created and printed during inspection to reflect consumer advisory disclosure and statement with items asterisked.

out_items.name: Compliance with variance, specialized process, HACCP

violations.title: Variance Requirement, Health Department Determines Need
violations.observation: Specialized processing method of food preparation for SOU VIDE.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall obtain a variance from the Regulatory Authority as specified in 8-103.10 and under 8-103.11 before: 1. smoking food as a method of food preservation rather than as a method for flavor enhancement, 2. curing food, 3. using food additives or adding components such as vinegar, 4. packaging food using a Reduced Oxygen Packaging method, 5. operating a molluscan shellfish life-support system display tank used to store and display shellfish that are offered for human consumption, 6. custom processing animals that are for personal use as food and not for sale or service in a food establishment, 7. preparing food by another method that is determined by the Regularty Authority to require a variance or, 8. sprouting seeds or beans. -Discussed variance requirements for kimchi and sou vide with manager present. Manager indicated these processes will be discontinued.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: utensils and rice scoop at cookline observed in container of ambient water
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. -utensils taken to wash rinse and sanitize and returned to cookline.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: 1 Dr countertop observed at 65F
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. TCS foods removed from unit.
